digest.en: Pakistan's 'Marka-e-Haq Day' announcement leads. Dua Lipa's lawsuit against Samsung over image use follows. Online creators are reshaping Africa's news.
digest.hi: पश्चिम बंगाल में आयुष्मान भारत योजना का लागू होना इस समय की प्रमुख खबर है। यह केंद्र की स्वास्थ्य पहल को राज्य में एकीकृत करने का एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है। इसके साथ ही, पश्चिम एशिया संकट के बीच अदाणी द्वारा AI और डेटा सेंटर पर जोर देना भविष्य की ओर एक संकेत है।

articles.title: Pakistan PM announces to celebrate May 10 as ‘Marka-e-Haq Day’ every year
articles.summary: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced May 10 Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif claimed that Pakistani armed forces gave a "historic and befitting response" to the enemy, he said while addressing a ceremony on May 10, 2026, to mark the first anniversary of 'Marka-e-Haq'. Pakistan PM announces to celebrate May 10 as ‘Marka-e-Haq Day’ every year.

articles.title: Dua Lipa sues Samsung for US$15 million for allegedly using her image to sell TVs
articles.summary: Dua Lipa sued Samsung for US$15 million. The lawsuit alleges that Samsung featured a copyrighted image of the singer on the front of cardboard boxes containing televisions for retail sale, enabling the company to benefit from what seemed like her endorsement of the product. Dua Lipa sues Samsung for US$15 million for allegedly using her image to sell TVs.

articles.title: Film paints vision of a post-coup Brazil giving up rainforest
articles.summary: A fictional film depicts Brazil in 2025 following a successful rightwing coup. The plot shows the assassination of the president and the closure of congress. The new government then cedes control of the Amazon rainforest to the United States. The film highlights threats to Indigenous peoples.

articles.title: Tehran, Taiwan, trade … what are the hazards facing Trump on Xi summit tightrope?
articles.summary: Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a summit with Chinese US leader enters talks with superpower rival from vulnerable position, but will be hoping for economic wins amid turbulent backdropIf all goes to plan over the next few days – and that is a big if – Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a highly anticipated summit with Xi Jinping, China’s leader. The trip will mark the first time a US president has visited China in nearly a decade.

articles.title: Indonesian rescuers retrieve body from Mount Dukono as search continues
articles.summary: Indonesian rescuers recovered the body of a woman after a volcanic eruption on Mount Woman recovered after volcanic eruption on remote island, while operation to find two missing Singaporeans goes onRescuers have recovered the body of an Indonesian woman who was caught in a volcanic eruption on Mount Dukono on Indonesia’s remote island of Halmahera, officials have said. Search operations continued on Saturday for the bodies of two Singaporeans.

articles.title: ‘Watching us is like watching a cousin’: the online creators reshaping Africa’s news ecosphere
articles.summary: Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa posted a TikTok video explaining a dispute between the South African and Rwandan presidents. She detailed the roles of various South African groups in a conflict. Jaxa's content focuses on current affairs for a South African audience. Africa is leading a change in news consumption habits – and transforming the lives of current affairs enthusiastsLast year Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa posted a TikTok video about South African peacekeepers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

articles.title: Guardian reporter and colleagues detained and beaten by Somali police
articles.summary: Guardian reporter Mohamed Bulbul was detained and beaten by Somali police in Mogadishu. He was arrested with two colleagues, Abdihafid Nor Barre and Abdishakur Mohamed Moh. The arrests followed Bulbul's reporting for the Guardian on the alleged torture of a woman in prison.

articles.title: Central African Republic: Funding cuts put humanitarian support at risk
articles.summary: Funding cuts threaten humanitarian operations in the Central African Republic. The Central African Republic (CAR) is making progress towards stability and security but major aid budget cuts threaten humanitarian operations there, a senior official with the UN aid coordination office OCHA said on Friday in New York.

articles.title: Wider hantavirus outbreak risk is ‘absolutely low’, insists UN health agency
articles.summary: The World Health Organization stated the risk of hantavirus spreading beyond the current cluster is very low. A flight attendant who had contact with an infected passenger tested negative for the disease. The passenger, from a cruise ship outbreak, later died.

articles.title: Three hikers dead after Indonesia’s Mount Dukono volcano erupts
articles.summary: Three hikers, two Singaporean and one Indonesian, died on Halmahera island after Mount Dukono erupted. They were in a restricted area when the volcano ejected an ash cloud approximately 10 kilometers high. No nearby villages were affected by the eruption.

articles.title: Hong Kong dissident Nathan Law on China spies in UK: ‘We’re not surprised’
articles.summary: Hong Kong dissident Nathan Law stated he was unsurprised by reports of Chinese spies in the UK. The conviction of two men for spying, who had photographed Law, raises serious concerns about their access to sensitive information. Law lives with a bounty from Chinese authorities.
